column11: judgement: Novartis gives only a floor, first planned submission 2029 or later (Q2 2026 6-K 0001114448-26-000012), and no Phase 3 is registered; the platform study completes 2028-11-27 (NCT06947993). Reused from remibrutinib, Novartis's latest immunology approval to come from a Phase 2b: its dose-finding study in chronic spontaneous urticaria (NCT03926611) completed 2021-01-14, its first Phase 3 (REMIX-1, NCT05030311) started 2021-11-30, and FDA approved Rhapsido on 2025-09-30 (NDA218436, openFDA), 56.5 months after the Phase 2b completed. The same 56.5 months from 2028-11-27 is August 2033, which makes 2034 the first full year
column12: Case for earlier: Novartis waited for 52-week Phase 3 safety before filing remibrutinib, and J&J's icotrokinra took 39 months over the same stretch (the analogue JNJ-95597528 carries), which would give 2032. Case for later: a platform study screens compounds, so GHZ339 may need a dose-ranging Phase 2b of its own before Phase 3
